description: Send one email your app owes a person: a receipt, a sign-in link, a password reset. `mailboxId` is where it leaves from: a mailbox whose purpose is transactional (update_mailbox), or a sender address on one of your mail domains (create_sender_address), which sends through Amazon SES. It goes exactly as you wrote it: no signature, no unsubscribe line, no tracking, no wait between emails. Pass `fromName` to set the name on the From line of this one email, such as Acme Support: 1 to 64 characters on one line, without @, < or >. The From address stays the mailbox's or sender address's own. Pass `unsubscribeUrl`, your app's own unsubscribe link for this person, so mail apps like Gmail can show an unsubscribe button. It goes out as the `List-Unsubscribe` header, with `List-Unsubscribe-Post: List-Unsubscribe=One-Click`. When the person presses the button, the mail app sends a POST to your link, which must unsubscribe them with no other step. Use an https:// link of up to 995 ASCII characters, without spaces, commas, < or >. Your app records the unsubscribe: we add nothing to our suppression list. Pass `fileIds` to attach stored files from a mailbox you connected with its own mail server (409 `filesNotFromOurServers` from a sender address or through our mail servers; 409 `messageTooLargeForMailbox` past the mailbox's size limit). Pass `attachments` to send a calendar file (.ics) or a PDF with it, from a sender address or a mailbox: up to 3 files (10 with `fileIds`), a PDF up to 1 MB, a calendar file up to 256 KB, and the email with its files up to 2 MB. We read each file's bytes, not only its type and name, and any other kind of file is refused with a 400 that names the file and the rule. A calendar file may say METHOD:REQUEST, METHOD:CANCEL or METHOD:PUBLISH, or name no method; with one of the three it goes as an invitation, so Gmail and Outlook show their add-to-calendar card. From a sender address, the links in a calendar file are checked like the links in the body; we never read inside a PDF, so its links are not checked. On MCP a whole call is capped at 1 MB. Each file is kept as a stored file: list_files shows it, it counts toward the workspace's file room (409 `fileStorageFull` when that is full), and it is deleted 7 days after the email goes. It is refused, and nothing is sent, when the address stopped this kind of email (it bounced, or the person marked one as spam), when today's room is used up (429: `details.scope` says which, `resetAt` says when to try again), or when the workspace's plan has no transactional email or its payment failed (402). An unsubscribe from your campaigns does not stop it. intentKey is required, and it names one email. Send the identical request again, expiresAt, fromName, unsubscribeUrl, fileIds and attachments included, and you get that send back as it is now, and nothing more is sent. So a retry must resend exactly the same request. The same intentKey with a different email is refused (422). Pass expiresAt for a code or link that stops working: if it hasn't started going out by then, its status becomes `cancelled`, with errorCode `expired`, and it is never sent. From a sender address, `sent` means Amazon SES accepted the email (`viaOurServers` is true), not that it reached an inbox. send.delivered or send.bounced follow when the receiving server answers. expiresAt can't stop an email Amazon SES already accepted. SES replaces the delivered Message-ID and Date; our messageId stays on the ledger and SES's id is providerMessageId. From a mailbox, replies land in its Inbox, or at replyTo. From a sender address, they go to replyTo, or else to the reply-to address it was made with. A 429 from a sender address with `details.scope` `domainRamp`, `ipCeiling` or `ipShare` is about our shared Amazon SES sending room, not your plan, and nothing was reserved. Then, if another address of yours is already connected for transactional email, the same content can go through that `mailboxId` with its own intentKey: the person sees that address as the From. Never do this for an email that already went out (`sent` or `unknown`). Set it up before you need it: /docs/transactional#second-way-to-send. Without a second address, send the identical request again after `resetAt`. With `hostedTransactionalDay`, wait for `resetAt`: that is your workspace's number for the day. The answer is the send as reserved. To see how it went, send the identical request again, call get_send (it needs the `read` permission), or watch send.sent, send.failed, send.bounced and send.cancelled. An owner may limit the API key you call with: to some mailboxes or campaigns, to outreach or transactional email, and to a number of emails a day or in all. Anything outside those limits answers 403 and nothing is sent: `details.scope` names the limit (`keyMailbox`, `keyCampaign`, `keyStream` or `keyTotal`). When the key has sent all its emails for today, it answers 429 with `details.scope: "keyDay"`, `resetAt` and a Retry-After header. A key can't read or change its own limits: ask a workspace owner.

attachments.description: Files the email carries, in order: up to 3, each a calendar file (.ics) or a PDF, and the email with its files up to 2 MB. A calendar file may say METHOD:REQUEST, METHOD:CANCEL or METHOD:PUBLISH, or name no method. With one of the three it goes as an invitation, so Gmail and Outlook show their add-to-calendar card. No other kind of file is taken.

content.description: The file's bytes, in base64: a PDF up to 1 MB, a calendar file up to 256 KB. We read them to check the type: a PDF starts with %PDF-, and a calendar file is UTF-8 text with no NUL byte from BEGIN:VCALENDAR to END:VCALENDAR.

contentType.description: text/calendar for a calendar file, or application/pdf for a PDF.

filename.description: The file's name, like invite.ics or receipt-1042.pdf, up to 255 characters. It ends in .ics for a calendar file and .pdf for a PDF. A folder part such as C:\files\ is dropped.

bodyHtml.description: The HTML part, sent as given. Send bodyHtml, bodyText or both.

bodyText.description: The plain-text part, sent as given. Send bodyHtml, bodyText or both.

expiresAt.description: If it hasn't started going out by this moment (an ISO 8601 date and time with its offset), its status becomes `cancelled`, with errorCode `expired`, and it is never sent. Use it for a sign-in code or a link that stops working.

fileIds.description: Stored files to attach, in order, up to 10 ids from create_file or create_file_upload. A repeated id counts once.

fromName.description: The name on the From line of this one email, such as Acme Support: 1 to 64 characters on one line, without @, < or >. The From address stays the mailbox's or sender address's own. Left out, the email uses the name the mailbox or sender address already has.

idempotencyKey.description: Your own id for this one call, such as a UUID, up to 255 characters. If the call fails with no answer, call again with the same key and the same arguments: within 24 hours, a saved answer comes back instead of a second run. A call left unanswered can run again after 15 minutes, so a send also keeps its intentKey or draft revision.

intentKey.description: Your own name for this one email, up to 255 characters. Send the identical request again, expiresAt included, and you get the same send back, never a second email, with no time limit. The same intentKey with a different email is refused (422). Names starting with draft:, warmup: or campaign: are refused.

mailboxId.description: Where it leaves from: a mailbox whose purpose is transactional (update_mailbox), or a sender address (create_sender_address), which sends through Amazon SES.

replyTo.description: Where replies go, when it isn't the mailbox itself: an address someone reads. Left out, the mailbox's own Reply-To, or its address. A sender address has no inbox, so left out its replies go to the reply-to address it was made with.

to.description: The one person it goes to.

toName.description: Their name, for the To line.

unsubscribeUrl.description: Your app's own unsubscribe link for this person, such as https://app.example/unsubscribe?t=abc. It goes out as the `List-Unsubscribe` header, with `List-Unsubscribe-Post: List-Unsubscribe=One-Click`, so mail apps like Gmail can show an unsubscribe button. When the person presses it, the mail app sends a POST to your link, which must unsubscribe them with no other step. Use an https:// link of up to 995 ASCII characters, without spaces, commas, < or >. Your app records the unsubscribe: we add nothing to our suppression list. Left out, the email has no unsubscribe headers.
